subject: Clarify: penetration engagement asset buckets across hosting variants
messages:
From: Acme Security <audit@acmesecurity.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on assets in-scope for upcoming pentest engagement

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for scheduling the pentest for NimbleApps next month. Before we finalize the statement of work, we need to confirm exactly which ‘asset buckets’ you consider in-scope across Redwood hosting variants. Specifically:

- Hosted (Redwood API) customers: which shared services and management plane endpoints are we allowed to test?
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): are tenant-side connectors, sidecars, and customer-managed NFS mounts included?
- Private / VPC / on-prem: do we test customer-controlled network endpoints or only Redwood control plane components?

Can you also point us to any network ranges, bastion hosts, or temporary test credentials you want us to use? We prefer to lock scope now to avoid submitting later exclusions.

Attached is our usual scoping checklist — please mark what is allowed/disallowed for each hosting model and return.

Thanks,
John Doe
Engagement Lead, Acme Security

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: NimbleApps Security Ops <security@nimbleapps.com>
Date: Mon, 13 May 2028 10:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on assets in-scope for upcoming pentest engagement

Hi John — thanks for the checklist. High level guidance below to help your scoping matrix; I'll follow up with our security and infra teams for precise inventory and IPs.

Quick summary (please treat this as preliminary — final confirmation after internal review):

- Hosted (Redwood API):
  - In-scope: Redwood-managed API endpoints that process tenant requests (control plane and data plane components we operate).
  - Out-of-scope: Shared third-party dependencies (e.g., external SaaS integrations) unless they are invoked directly via Redwood endpoints in a way that would affect tenant data.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity):
  - In-scope: Redwood-hosted GPU nodes, dedicated routing fabric, and any Redwood-sidecar processes we deploy into the reserved pool.
  - Possibly in-scope: customer-managed sidecars/connectors only if they run inside Redwood-managed networks and we have explicit approval from the customer to test them.

- Private / VPC / On-prem:
  - In-scope: Redwood control plane components (where present) and any Redwood-delivered agents.
  - Out-of-scope: customer-owned networks and endpoints that we do not manage or that are behind their private firewalls unless the customer explicitly requests inclusion.

Next steps: I will loop in Rishi (security) and Laura (infra) to provide the inventory file and indicate where we require NimbleApps’ authorization to include tenant-side artifacts.

Regards,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Chloe — hi. Quick answers and clarifications from security/infra perspective:

- Dedicated:
  - Tenant-side connectors / marketplace sidecars: default is OUT-OF-SCOPE unless the customer explicitly opts-in and provides written authorization. If the sidecar runs inside a Redwood-managed network namespace and we deploy the image, we can include it, but we need the customer to sign the scoping matrix to accept the risk and provide test creds.
  - Redwood-managed sidecars (ship-with-cluster for monitoring/kv): IN-SCOPE.

- Hosted API:
  - In-scope: control plane endpoints that accept tenant tokens, the public ingestion edge, and any data-plane components we operate.
  - Out-of-scope: the multi-tenant metadata store that is operated by a third party vendor — we'll need vendor permission to test that.

- Private / VPC / On-prem:
  - Only Redwood-delivered agents and control-plane connectors are in-scope. Customer-owned services, private subnets, and on-prem storage are out-of-scope unless the customer requests and signs off.

Inventory and artifacts: attached network-environment-inventory.csv (includes Dedicated cluster CIDR blocks and management bastion FQDNs). I also included a short checklist of what credentials we can provide for the engagement and how long they remain valid.

Attachments: network-environment-inventory.csv, pen-test-scoping-matrix-v1.pdf

Let me know if Acme needs temporary test users for the NimbleApps Dedicated pool — we can issue them for a 72-hour window and audit after.

-Rishi
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final scope confirmation for NimbleApps pentest (per Acme request)

Hi John / Acme team — thanks for the patience. Confirming the agreed scope for NimbleApps engagement below; please treat this as the official scoping decision for the SOW.

1) Hosted (Redwood API): IN-SCOPE — Redwood-managed public API endpoints, control plane services that process tenant requests, and Redwood-deployed data-plane workers.
2) Dedicated (Reserved capacity): IN-SCOPE — Redwood-hosted GPU nodes, routing fabric, and Redwood-managed sidecars.
   - Tenant-installed marketplace sidecars / customer-managed connectors: OUT-OF-SCOPE unless NimbleApps signs the attached opt-in form.
3) Private / VPC / On-prem: IN-SCOPE ONLY for Redwood-delivered agents and control-plane connectors. Customer-owned networks and storage are OUT-OF-SCOPE unless NimbleApps requests inclusion in writing.

Attachments included for the engagement: pen-test-scoping-matrix-v1.pdf, network-environment-inventory.csv.

Action items:
- Acme: please return a signed scoping matrix that notes any tenant-side artifacts you want to include (we will not include them by default).
- NimbleApps: if you opt to include any customer-managed sidecars, please confirm by EOD next Tuesday and provide test credentials.

Links / evidence: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-scoping (inventory + agent binaries)

Thanks — Chloe
